findings.text: The merge keeps the node's inline no-pointer branch in crew_complete after main's _refuse_a_landing_without_its_pointer call at :3507, which raises for the same condition before this branch can be reached: reckon/crew/runs.py:1081-1096 raises for a missing, malformed or non-object pointer, so the branch is reachable only for a pointer file holding an empty object. It is dead code, and the distinction it drew is lost - main's helper names a pending landing record path in its message whether or not a record exists, so a run with neither a pointer nor a record is now told to look at a file that is not there. The goal behaviour (refuse before writing, leave the record standing) is still delivered by the earlier refusal, which is why this does not hold the node.

The helper builds the pending record path inline as pending_landing.pending_dir() / f"{run_id}.json" instead of calling the accessor at reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:60. This is the one resolution of that path the module owns, and this node's repair exists precisely because a second spelling of it drifted: if the record's filename or directory changes, _record_path moves and this refusal goes on naming the default path, so the message points a coordinator at a record the pass no longer reads.
